entries.scope: Any x-only, Kummer, even-theta, y^2, or sign-erasing orbit-norm observable claimed to equal direct canonical scalar parity on an odd prime-order cycle.
entries.reason: Direct parity is anti-invariant under Q -> -Q and therefore cannot factor through x(Q).
entries.reopen_condition: Change the output to a correctly transformed residual bit or introduce explicit orientation data and charge it.

entries.scope: Finite products or ratios of fixed-index transported division-polynomial or elliptic-net observables.
entries.reason: Their quadratic exponent defect is balanced and does not expose the absolute EDS residue by that mechanism alone.
entries.reopen_condition: Provide a nonlocal or index-growing mechanism with an exact unbalanced transformation law and full charged cost.

entries.scope: Globally linear translation representations or fixed theta spaces directly representing canonical parity around an odd cycle.
entries.reason: The parity cut has full Fourier support and forces linear-size representation dimension in the stated model.
entries.reopen_condition: Use a nonlinear, non-global, generator-sensitive circuit outside the declared linear model.

entries.scope: Regular rational functions directly outputting plus/minus one parity on all group points, or residual signs on the Kummer line, under the stated regularity assumptions.
entries.reason: The declared direct interpolation models require degree linear in n.
entries.reopen_condition: Exhibit a short high-degree straight-line program or a representation whose construction and evaluation avoid linear charged cost.

entries.scope: A norm-n Eisenstein-CM element decomposed into two proper positive-degree endomorphism or isogeny stages when n is prime.
entries.reason: The positive integer stage degrees multiply to prime n, so one stage has degree one.
entries.reopen_condition: Use compact evaluation of the full map, transposed evaluation, local data, modular composition, or a non-factor-chain circuit.

entries.scope: Any claim that degree about n by itself implies arithmetic-circuit size about n or sqrt(n).
entries.reason: Repeated squaring produces exponentially high degree with logarithmic straight-line-program length.
entries.reopen_condition: Add a stronger invariant such as support, orientation information, advice, representation construction, or a restricted gate model.

entries.scope: Consecutive-segment summaries whose visible state is only two endpoint values and whose composition is additive with a constant defect.
entries.reason: The segment value collapses to endpoint data plus a fixed defect in the declared grammar.
entries.reopen_condition: Introduce nonlocal state, nonlinear coupling, or explicitly growing shared state and charge it.

entries.scope: Consecutive-segment summaries represented as an ordered product conjugated by endpoint basis values, with no additional hidden state.
entries.reason: The declared product grammar reduces to endpoint conjugation and does not independently select the absolute orientation.
entries.reopen_condition: Compose both orientation branches simultaneously or add a genuinely nonmultiplicative primitive with charged state growth.

entries.scope: A quadratic character of one classical terminal Miller function f_(m,P), for arbitrary positive index m, or an explicit product of too few independent terminal functions.
entries.reason: The terminal divisor m[P]-[mP]-(m-1)[O] has at most two odd-support slots after reduction modulo two, independently of the Miller-loop length.
entries.reopen_condition: Use a recursively shared object that is not an explicit product of terminal Miller functions, or leave the one-rational-character model.

entries.scope: Any unrestricted claim that square-root-scale odd divisor support alone implies square-root field-operation or straight-line-program cost.
entries.reason: Division polynomials have odd support quadratic in the index while their standard doubling recurrences have logarithmic dependency depth and a constant-width window per level.
entries.reopen_condition: Add a restricted gate model or another invariant that rules out division-polynomial-style recurrence compression.

entries.scope: An unchanged formula chi(psi_m(Q)) claimed to equal canonical parity across a transfer corpus containing fields with q congruent to both 1 and 3 modulo 4.
entries.reason: Odd m is invariant under Q -> -Q. Even m remains character-invariant when chi(-1)=+1, while canonical parity is always anti-invariant on an odd cycle.
entries.reopen_condition: Specialize to q congruent to 3 modulo 4 with even m, add a charged covariance-correcting factor, or leave the pure division-polynomial character model.

entries.scope: One global phase times one classical quadratic character chi(psi_m(Q)), for an arbitrary positive index m, on the secp256k1 prime-order subgroup.
entries.reason: Odd indices fail negation covariance. Every admissible even index m=2u collapses in square class to chi(psi_2([u]Q)); the published 6*sqrt(p) subgroup Fourier bound is far below the exact parity peak. Independent Paley-tournament and psi_3 all-residue completion arguments give separate large-order certificates.
entries.reopen_condition: Use products or ratios of multiple independently pulled factors, a field-valued output without one outer character, adaptive branching, or another mechanism outside the single classical psi_m character model.

entries.scope: One global phase times chi(psi_m(Q)) on each curve of the declared eighteen-curve transfer corpus, with arbitrary positive m and no per-point advice.
entries.reason: The published 6*sqrt(q) Fourier inequality closes fourteen curves; exhaustive scans of every invertible multiplier class and both global phases close the remaining four. The independent covariance and Paley checks agree on their respective congruence classes.
entries.reopen_condition: Change the corpus or leave the pure single-factor division-polynomial character class.

global_warning: Every entry is scoped. The pure single classical division-polynomial character is closed on secp256k1 and on the declared eighteen-curve corpus, but products or ratios of multiple factors, direct field-valued Y_G evaluation and unrestricted arithmetic circuits remain open. This registry is not a proof that UORC-056 has no sub-root evaluator.
